translations.literal: Earlier, near the end of Gao Huan's life, he had charged Gao Cheng: "If Hou Jing rebels, Murong Shaozong should be the one to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, near the end of Gao Huan's life, he had charged Gao Cheng: "If Hou Jing rebels, Murong Shaozong should be the one to meet him.

sentences.zh: 」至是，竟立功效。

translations.literal: " At this time he indeed established merit.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time he indeed established merit.

sentences.zh: 西魏遣其大將王思政入據潁州，又以紹宗為南道行臺，與太尉高岳、儀同劉豐等率軍圍擊，堰洧水以灌之。

translations.literal: Western Wei dispatched its great general Wang Sizheng to enter and hold Ying Province; Shaozong was again made southern-circuit mobile-office commissioner and, with Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Palace Attendant Equal in Rank Liu Feng, and others, led troops to besiege and attack, damming the Wei River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei dispatched its great general Wang Sizheng to enter and hold Ying Province; Shaozong was again made southern-circuit mobile-office commissioner and, with Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Palace Attendant Equal in Rank Liu Feng, and others, led troops to besiege and attack, damming the Wei River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 時紹宗頻有兇夢，意每惡之。

translations.literal: At that time Shaozong repeatedly had ominous dreams, and his mind was always ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shaozong repeatedly had ominous dreams, and his mind was always ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 乃私謂左右曰：「吾自年二十已還，恒有蒜發，昨來蒜發忽然自盡。

translations.literal: He privately said to those close to him: "From the age of twenty onward I have always had white hair; yesterday my white hair suddenly vanished altogether.
translations.idiomatic: He privately said to those close to him: "From the age of twenty onward I have always had white hair; yesterday my white hair suddenly vanished altogether.

sentences.zh: 以理推之，蒜者算也，吾算將盡乎？

translations.literal: By reason I infer: white hair is suan — is my allotted span at an end?
translations.idiomatic: By reason I infer: suan means 'allotted span' — is my allotted span at an end?

sentences.zh: 」未幾，與豐臨堰，見北有塵氣，乃入艦同坐。

translations.literal: " Before long, he and Feng were at the dam and saw dust rising in the north; they entered a warship and sat together.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long, he and Feng were at the dam and saw dust rising in the north; they entered a warship and sat together.

sentences.zh: 暴風從東北來，遠近晦冥，舟纜斷，飄艦徑向敵城。

translations.literal: A violent wind came from the northeast; near and far were dark and obscure; the boat cables snapped, and the drifting ship was borne straight toward the enemy city.
translations.idiomatic: A violent wind came from the northeast; near and far were dark and obscure; the boat cables snapped, and the drifting ship was borne straight toward the enemy city.

sentences.zh: 紹宗自度不免，遂投水而死，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Shaozong judged that he could not escape; he threw himself into the water and died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong judged that he could not escape; he threw himself into the water and died, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 三軍將士莫不悲惋，朝廷嗟傷。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the three armies all mourned in grief; the court sighed in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers of the three armies all mourned in grief; the court sighed in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、二青、二兗、齊、濟、光七州軍事、尚書令、太尉、青州刺史，謚曰景惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs in the two Qing, two Yan, Qi, Ji, and Guang provinces, director of the masters of writing, grand commandant, and governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs in the two Qing, two Yan, Qi, Ji, and Guang provinces, director of the masters of writing, grand commandant, and governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 除其長子士肅為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shisu was appointed attendant cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shisu was appointed attendant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋以謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以紹宗功，罪止士肅身。

translations.literal: Because of Shaozong's merit, the court limited punishment to Shisu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Shaozong's merit, the court limited punishment to Shisu alone.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配饗世宗廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given place in the ancestral temple of Gao Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given place in the ancestral temple of Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 士肅弟建中，襲紹宗爵。

translations.literal: Shisu's younger brother Jianzhong inherited Shaozong's title.
translations.idiomatic: Shisu's younger brother Jianzhong inherited Shaozong's title.

sentences.zh: 武平末，儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping, he reached palace attendant equal in rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping, he reached palace attendant equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，大將軍、疊州總管。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was great general and area commander of Die Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was great general and area commander of Die Province.

sentences.zh: 薛脩義

translations.literal: Xue Xiuyi
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiuyi

sentences.zh: 薛脩義，字公讓，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Xiuyi, styled Gongrang, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiuyi, styled Gongrang, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖紹，魏七兵尚書、太子太保。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shao was Wei minister of the seven armies and grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao was Wei minister of the seven armies and grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 祖壽仁，河東河北二郡守、秦州刺史、汾陰公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouren was governor of the two commanderies of Hedong and Hebei, governor of Qin Province, and Duke of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouren was governor of the two commanderies of Hedong and Hebei, governor of Qin Province, and duke of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 父寶集，定陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Baoji was governor of Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Baoji was governor of Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 脩義少而姦俠，輕財重氣，招召豪猾，時有急難相奔投者，多能容匿之。

translations.literal: Xiuyi from youth was cunning and chivalrous, lightly spending wealth and valuing spirit; he summoned bold and lawless men, and when men in urgent distress came to him for refuge, he often sheltered them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi from youth was cunning and chivalrous, lightly spending wealth and valuing bold spirit; he summoned bold and lawless men, and when men in urgent distress came to him for refuge, he often sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 魏咸陽王為司州牧，用為法曹從事。

translations.literal: Prince Xianyang of Wei was governor of Si Province and employed him as legal bureau attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianyang of Wei was governor of Si Province and employed him as legal bureau attendant.

sentences.zh: 魏北海王顥鎮徐州，引為墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Beihai of Wei, Yuan Hao, garrisoned Xu Province and brought Xiuyi in as ink bureau adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Beihai of Wei, Yuan Hao, garrisoned Xu Province and brought Xiuyi in as ink bureau adjutant.

sentences.zh: 正光末，天下兵起，顥為征西將軍，都督華、豳、東秦諸軍事，兼左僕射、西道行臺，以脩義為統軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, when warfare rose throughout the realm, Hao was made general who campaigns west, area commander of Hua, Bin, and Eastern Qin military affairs, additionally left vice director and western-circuit mobile-office commissioner; Xiuyi was made area commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang, when warfare rose throughout the realm, Hao was made general who campaigns west, area commander of Hua, Bin, and Eastern Qin military affairs, additionally left vice director and western-circuit mobile-office commissioner; Xiuyi was made area commander.

sentences.zh: 時有詔，能募得三千人別將。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict: whoever could recruit three thousand men would be made separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was an edict: whoever could recruit three thousand men would be made separate commander.

sentences.zh: 於是脩義還河東，仍歷平陽、弘農諸郡，合得七千餘人，即假安北將軍、西道別將。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiuyi returned to Hedong and passed through the commanderies of Pingyang, Hongnong, and others, gathering more than seven thousand men in all; he was then provisionally made general who pacifies the north and separate commander of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xiuyi returned to Hedong and passed through the commanderies of Pingyang, Hongnong, and others, gathering more than seven thousand men in all; he was then provisionally made general who pacifies the north and separate commander of the western circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄而東西二夏、南北兩華及豳州等反叛，顥進討之。

translations.literal: Before long, Eastern and Western Xia, Northern and Southern Hua, and Bin Province and others rebelled; Hao advanced to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Eastern and Western Xia, Northern and Southern Hua, and Bin Province and others rebelled; Hao advanced to attack them.

sentences.zh: 脩義率所部，頗有功。

translations.literal: Xiuyi led his command and had considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi led his command and had considerable merit.

sentences.zh: 絳蜀賊陳雙熾等聚汾曲，詔脩義為大都督，與行臺長孫稚共討之。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Shu bandits Chen Shuangchi and others gathered along the Fen River bend; an edict made Xiuyi grand commander and, with Mobile-Office Commissioner Zhangsun Zhi, jointly attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Shu bandits Chen Shuangchi and others gathered along the Fen River bend; an edict made Xiuyi grand commander and, with Mobile-Office Commissioner Zhangsun Zhi, jointly attacked them.

sentences.zh: 脩義以雙熾是其鄉人，遂輕詣壘下，曉以利害，熾等遂降。

translations.literal: Xiuyi, because Shuangchi was a fellow townsman, went lightly to the foot of the fortress and explained advantage and harm; Chi and the others thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi, because Shuangchi was a fellow townsman, went lightly to the foot of the fortress and explained advantage and harm; Chi and the others thereupon surrendered.

sentences.zh: 拜脩義龍門鎮將。

translations.literal: Xiuyi was appointed garrison commander of Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi was appointed garrison commander of Longmen.

sentences.zh: 後脩義宗人鳳賢等作亂，圍鎮城。

translations.literal: Later Xiuyi's clansman Fengxian and others raised disorder and besieged the garrison city.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiuyi's clansman Fengxian and others raised disorder and besieged the garrison city.

sentences.zh: 脩義亦以天下紛擾，規自縱擅，遂與鳳賢聚衆為逆，自號黃鉞大將軍。

translations.literal: Xiuyi too, because the realm was in turmoil, planned to act on his own authority; he joined Fengxian in gathering a crowd in rebellion and styled himself Great General of the Yellow Axe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi too, because the realm was in turmoil, planned to act on his own authority; he joined Fengxian in gathering a crowd in rebellion and styled himself Great General of the Yellow Axe.

sentences.zh: 詔都督宗正珍孫討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Area Commander Zong Zheng Zhensun attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Area Commander Zong Zheng Zhensun attack him.

sentences.zh: 軍未至，脩義慚悔，乃遣其帳下孫懷彥奉表自陳，乞一大將招慰。

translations.literal: Before the army arrived, Xiuyi felt shame and regret; he sent his tent officer Sun Huaiyan to submit a memorial explaining himself and begging for a great general to come and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army arrived, Xiuyi felt shame and regret; he sent his tent officer Sun Huaiyan to submit a memorial explaining himself and begging for a great general to come and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 魏孝明遣西北大行臺胡元吉奉詔曉喻，脩義降。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming of Wei dispatched Northwestern Grand Commissioner Hu Yuanji with an edict to instruct and explain; Xiuyi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming of Wei dispatched Northwestern Grand Commissioner Hu Yuanji with an edict to instruct and explain; Xiuyi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 鳳賢等猶據險屯結，長孫稚軍於弘農，珍孫軍靈橋，未能進。

translations.literal: Fengxian and others still held the heights and entrenched themselves; Zhangsun Zhi's army was at Hongnong and Zhensun's army at Lingqiao, and neither could advance.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian and others still held the heights and entrenched themselves; Zhangsun Zhi's army was at Hongnong and Zhensun's army at Lingqiao, and neither could advance.

sentences.zh: 脩義與其從叔善樂、從弟嘉族等各率義勇為攻取之勢，與鳳賢書示其禍福。

translations.literal: Xiuyi, with his father's younger brother Shanle and his younger cousin Jiazu and others, each led righteous warriors to create the momentum of attack and capture, and sent Fengxian a letter showing fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi, with his father's younger brother Shanle and his younger cousin Jiazu and others, each led righteous warriors to create the momentum of attack and capture, and sent Fengxian a letter showing fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 鳳賢降，拜鳳賢龍驤將軍、假節、稷山鎮將，夏陽縣子、邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Fengxian surrendered; Fengxian was appointed general of soaring dragon, bearer of the staff of authority, garrison commander of Jishan, and Viscount of Xiayang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian surrendered; Fengxian was appointed general of soaring dragon, bearer of the staff of authority, garrison commander of Jishan, and viscount of Xiayang County with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 封脩義汾陰縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Xiuyi was enfeoffed Marquis of Fenyin County with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi was enfeoffed marquis of Fenyin County with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮以脩義豪猾反覆，錄送晉陽，與高昂等並見拘防。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, because Xiuyi was bold, lawless, and changeable, had him sent under guard to Jinyang and detained together with Gao Ang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, because Xiuyi was bold, lawless, and changeable, had him sent under guard to Jinyang and detained together with Gao Ang and others.

sentences.zh: 榮赴洛，以脩義等自隨，置於駝牛署。

translations.literal: When Rong went to Luoyang, he took Xiuyi and the others with him and placed them in the camel-and-ox office.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong went to Luoyang, he took Xiuyi and the others with him and placed them in the camel-and-ox office.

sentences.zh: 榮死，魏孝莊以脩義為弘農、河北、河東、正平四郡大都督。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei made Xiuyi grand commander of the four commanderies of Hongnong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei made Xiuyi grand commander of the four commanderies of Hongnong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 時高祖為晉州刺史，見脩義，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan was governor of Jin Province; when he saw Xiuyi he treated him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan was governor of Jin Province; when he saw Xiuyi he treated him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱兆立魏長廣王為主，除脩義右將軍、陜州刺史，假安南將軍。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao enthroned the Prince of Changguang of Wei, Xiuyi was appointed right general and governor of Shan Province, provisionally made general who pacifies the south.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao enthroned the Prince of Changguang of Wei, Xiuyi was appointed right general and governor of Shan Province, provisionally made general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 魏前廢帝初，以脩義為持節、後將軍、南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the deposed emperor of Wei, Xiuyi was made bearer of the staff of authority, rear general, and governor of Southern Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the deposed emperor of Wei, Xiuyi was made bearer of the staff of authority, rear general, and governor of Southern Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖起義信都，破四胡於韓陵，遣徵脩義，從至晉陽，以脩義行幷州事。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu and defeated the Four Huns at Hanling, he dispatched a summons to Xiuyi; Xiuyi followed him to Jinyang, and Xiuyi was made acting governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu and defeated the Four Huns at Hanling, he dispatched a summons to Xiuyi; Xiuyi followed him to Jinyang, and Xiuyi was made acting governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 又從高祖平尒朱兆。

translations.literal: He also followed Gao Huan in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Gao Huan in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 武帝之入關也，高祖奉迎臨潼關，以脩義為關右行臺，自龍門濟河。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Gao Huan went to meet him at Lintong Pass and made Xiuyi mobile-office commissioner of the Guanxi circuit, crossing the Yellow River from Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Gao Huan went to meet him at Lintong Pass and made Xiuyi mobile-office commissioner of the Guanxi circuit, crossing the Yellow River from Longmen.

sentences.zh: 西魏北華州刺史薛崇禮屯楊氏壁，脩義以書招之，崇禮率萬餘人降。

translations.literal: Xue Chongli, governor of Northern Hua Province in Western Wei, garrisoned Yangshi Rampart; Xiuyi summoned him by letter, and Chongli led more than ten thousand men in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Chongli, governor of Northern Hua Province in Western Wei, garrisoned Yangshi Rampart; Xiuyi summoned him by letter, and Chongli led more than ten thousand men in surrender.

sentences.zh: 樊子鵠之據兗州，脩義從大司馬婁昭破平之。

translations.literal: When Fan Zihe held Yan Province, Xiuyi followed Grand Marshal Lou Zhao in breaking and pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zihe held Yan Province, Xiuyi followed Grand Marshal Lou Zhao in breaking and pacifying him.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除衛將軍、南中郎將，帶汲郡太守、頓丘、淮陽、東郡、黎陽五郡都督。

translations.literal: During Tianping, he was appointed guard general and southern cadre general, concurrently governor of Ji Commandery, and area commander of the five commanderies of Dunqiu, Huaiyang, Eastern, and Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping, he was appointed guard general and southern cadre general, concurrently governor of Ji Commandery, and area commander of the five commanderies of Dunqiu, Huaiyang, Eastern, and Liyang.

sentences.zh: 遷東徐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Eastern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 元象初，拜儀同。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was appointed palace attendant equal in rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was appointed palace attendant equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，從諸軍退。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Shaye, he withdrew with the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Shaye, he withdrew with the other armies.

sentences.zh: 還，行晉州事。

translations.literal: On return, he served as acting governor of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: On return, he served as acting governor of Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 封祖業棄城走，脩義追至洪洞，說祖業還守，而祖業不從。

translations.literal: Zu Ye abandoned the city and fled; Xiuyi pursued to Hongtong, urging Zu Ye to return and hold the city, but Zu Ye would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ye abandoned the city and fled; Xiuyi pursued to Hongtong, urging Zu Ye to return and hold the city, but Zu Ye would not obey.

sentences.zh: 脩義還據晉州，安集固守。

translations.literal: Xiuyi returned and held Jin Province, settling the people and defending firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi returned and held Jin Province, settling the people and defending firmly.

sentences.zh: 西魏儀同長孫子彥逼城下，脩義開門伏甲以待之，子彥不測虛實，於是遁去。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Ziyan, palace attendant equal in rank of Western Wei, pressed the city; Xiuyi opened the gate and hid armored troops to await him; Ziyan could not gauge truth and falsehood, and thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Ziyan, palace attendant equal in rank of Western Wei, pressed the city; Xiuyi opened the gate and hid armored troops to await him; Ziyan could not gauge truth and falsehood, and thereupon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚嘉之，就拜晉州刺史、南汾、東雍、陜四州行臺，賞帛千疋。

translations.literal: Gao Huan greatly praised him; on the spot he was appointed governor of Jin Province and mobile-office commissioner of Southern Fen, Eastern Yong, and Shan provinces, rewarded with a thousand rolls of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan greatly praised him; on the spot he was appointed governor of Jin Province and mobile-office commissioner of Southern Fen, Eastern Yong, and Shan provinces, rewarded with a thousand rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 脩義在州，擒西魏所署正平太守段榮顯。

translations.literal: While Xiuyi was in the province, he captured Duan Rongxian, governor of Zhengping appointed by Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiuyi was in the province, he captured Duan Rongxian, governor of Zhengping appointed by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 招降胡酋胡垂黎等部落數千口，表置五城郡以安處之。

translations.literal: He summoned and reduced the Hu chieftain Hu Chuili and other tribes, several thousand mouths in all, and memorialized to establish Wucheng Commandery to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned and reduced the Hu chieftain Hu Chuili and other tribes, several thousand mouths in all, and memorialized to establish Wucheng Commandery to settle them.

sentences.zh: 高仲密之叛，以脩義為西南道行臺，為掎角聲勢，不行。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Xiuyi was made southwestern-circuit mobile-office commissioner to create pincer momentum, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Xiuyi was made southwestern-circuit mobile-office commissioner to create pincer momentum, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋除齊州刺史，以黷貨除名。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Qi Province and, for corrupt acceptance of goods, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Qi Province and, for corrupt acceptance of goods, was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 追其前守晉州功，復其官爵，仍拜衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In recognition of his former merit in defending Jin Province, his offices and noble ranks were restored, and he was again appointed Minister of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his earlier merit in holding Jin Province, his offices and noble ranks were restored, and he was again appointed minister of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 時山胡侵亂晉州，遣脩義追討，破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Mountain Hu raided and harassed Jin Province; Xiuyi was dispatched to pursue and suppress them, and he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Mountain Hu raided Jin Province; Xiuyi was sent in pursuit, broke them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 進爵正平郡公，加開府。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Zhengping Commandery, with the seal of opening an office conferred.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was advanced to duke of Zhengping Commandery, and he was given the seal of opening an office.

sentences.zh: 世宗以高祖遺旨，減封二百戶，別封脩義為平鄉男。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, following the Grand Ancestor's dying charge, reduced his fief by two hundred households and separately enfeoffed Xiuyi as Baron of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, honoring the Grand Ancestor's dying charge, reduced the fief by two hundred households and separately enfeoffed Xiuyi as baron of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除護軍，別封藍田縣公，又拜太子太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was appointed protector of the army, separately enfeoffed Duke of Lantian County, and also made grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed protector of the army, separately enfeoffed duke of Lantian County, and also made grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 五年七月卒，時年七十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year he died, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈晉太華三州諸軍事、司空、晉州刺史，贈物三百段。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted military affairs of the three provinces of Jin, Tai, and Hua, Minister of Works, and governor of Jin Province, with three hundred bolts of goods given in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted military affairs over Jin, Tai, and Hua provinces, minister of works, and governor of Jin Province, with three hundred bolts of goods sent in tribute.

sentences.zh: 子文殊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wenshu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenshu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 薛嘉族

translations.literal: Xue Jiazu
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jiazu

sentences.zh: 脩義從弟嘉族，性亦豪爽。

translations.literal: Xiuyi's younger cousin Jiazu was likewise bold and forthright in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi's younger cousin Jiazu was likewise bold and open-handed in temperament.

sentences.zh: 釋褐員外散騎侍郎，稍遷正平太守。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was made supernumerary Gentleman-Attendant at the Dispersal of Horses, and was gradually promoted to governor of Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first taking office he was made supernumerary gentleman-attendant at the dispersal of horses, and was gradually promoted to governor of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖在信都，嘉族聞而赴義。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor was at Xindu, Jiazu heard and came to join the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor raised the cause at Xindu, Jiazu heard of it and came to join him.

sentences.zh: 從平四胡於韓陵，除華州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Four Huns at Hanling and was appointed governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the victory over the Four Huns at Hanling and was appointed governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳拒命，令嘉族置騎河上，以禦大軍。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue defied orders, Jiazu was ordered to post cavalry along the river to oppose the great army.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue defied orders, Jiazu was ordered to post cavalry along the river to hold back the main force.

sentences.zh: 嘉族遂棄其乘馬，浮河而度，歸於高祖。

translations.literal: Jiazu thereupon abandoned his riding horse, crossed the river by swimming, and returned to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazu thereupon abandoned his mount, swam the river, and returned to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 由是拜揚州刺史，卒於官。

translations.literal: Because of this he was appointed governor of Yang Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was appointed governor of Yang Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子震，字文雄。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, styled Wenhun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, styled Wenhun.

sentences.zh: 天平初，受旨鎮守龍門，陷於西魏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he received orders to garrison Longmen and was lost to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he received orders to hold Longmen and was taken by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 元象中，方得逃還。

translations.literal: During Yuanxiang he was able to escape and return.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanxiang he at last escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其至誠，除廣州刺史。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor praised his utmost loyalty and appointed him governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor praised his steadfast loyalty and appointed him governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 後從慕容紹宗討侯景，以功別封膚施縣男。

translations.literal: Later he followed Murong Shaozong in campaigning against Hou Jing and, for merit, was separately enfeoffed Baron of Fushi County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Murong Shaozong against Hou Jing and, for merit, was separately enfeoffed baron of Fushi County.

sentences.zh: 天保四年，從討山胡，破茹茹，並有功績，累遷譙州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, he followed in suppressing the Mountain Hu and breaking the Rouran, all with recorded merit, and was successively promoted to governor of Qiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao he followed campaigns against the Mountain Hu and the Rouran, winning merit in both, and was promoted in stages to governor of Qiao Province.

sentences.zh: 薛元穎

translations.literal: Xue Yuanying
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuanying

sentences.zh: 脩義從子元穎，父光熾，東雍州刺史、太常卿。

translations.literal: Xiuyi's nephew Yuanying — his father Guangchi was governor of Eastern Yong Province and minister of imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi's nephew Yuanying; his father Guangchi had been governor of Eastern Yong Province and minister of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元穎廉謹有信義，起家永安王參軍。

translations.literal: Yuanying was incorruptible, cautious, and trustworthy; he first took office as aide to the Prince of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying was incorruptible, careful, and trustworthy; he first entered service as aide to the Prince of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 行秀容縣事，有清名。

translations.literal: Acting in the affairs of Xiurong County, he earned a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: While acting in the affairs of Xiurong County, he won a name for clean government.

sentences.zh: 累轉定州別駕，舉清平勤幹，除漁陽太守。

translations.literal: After successive transfers he became vice-governor of Ding Province; recommended for integrity, fairness, and diligence, he was appointed governor of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: After successive transfers he became vice-governor of Ding Province; recommended for integrity, fairness, and diligence, he was appointed governor of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 叱列平

translations.literal: Chi Lieping
translations.idiomatic: Chi Lieping

sentences.zh: 叱列平，字殺鬼，代郡西部人也，世為酋帥。

translations.literal: Chi Lieping, styled Shagui, was a man of the western part of Dai Commandery; his family for generations were tribal chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Lieping, styled Shagui — Slayer of Demons — was a man of western Dai Commandery; his family had been tribal chieftains for generations.

sentences.zh: 平有容貌，美須髯，善騎射。

translations.literal: Ping had a striking appearance, with a fine beard and mustache, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was striking to look upon, with a handsome beard and mustache, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 襲第一領民酋長，臨江伯。

translations.literal: He inherited the post of first tribally enrolled chieftain and the title Baron of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the post of first tribally enrolled chieftain and the title baron of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，拔陵反叛，茹茹餘衆入寇馬邑，平以統軍屬，有戰功，補別將。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, Balang rebelled; Rouran remnant forces invaded Mayi; Ping served as a subordinate army commander, had battle merit, and was appointed separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiaochang, Balang rebelled and Rouran remnant bands raided Mayi; Ping served under the army commander, won distinction in battle, and was appointed separate commander.

sentences.zh: 後牧子作亂，劉胡侖、斛律可那律俱時構逆，以平為都督，討定胡侖等。

translations.literal: Later Muzhi raised disorder; Liu Hulu and Hulu Kenali both at the same time plotted rebellion; Ping was made area commander to suppress and settle Hulu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Later Muzhi stirred rebellion; Liu Hulu and Hulu Kenali rose together; Ping was made area commander to suppress Hulu and the rest.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊初，除武衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei's reign, he was appointed General of Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei's reign he was appointed general of martial guards.

sentences.zh: 隨尒朱榮破葛榮，平元顥，遷中軍都督、右衛將軍，封癭陶縣伯，邑七百戶。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in breaking Ge Rong and pacifying Yuan Hao, was transferred to commander of the central army and right guard general, enfeoffed Baron of Yingtao County with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong in breaking Ge Rong and pacifying Yuan Hao, was transferred to commander of the central army and right guard general, and enfeoffed baron of Yingtao County with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 榮死，平與榮妻及尒朱世隆等北走。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Ping fled north together with Rong's wife and Erzhu Shilong and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Ping fled north with Rong's wife and Erzhu Shilong and the others.

sentences.zh: 長廣王曄立，授右衛將軍，加京畿大都督。

translations.literal: When Prince Changguang Ye was enthroned, he was appointed right guard general and additionally made grand commander of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Changguang Ye was enthroned, he was appointed right guard general and additionally made grand commander of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時尒朱氏淩僭，平常慮危禍，會高祖起義，平遂歸誠。

translations.literal: At that time the Erzhu clan acted above their station; Ping often feared calamity; when the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous cause, Ping thereupon pledged his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Erzhu clan overreached; Ping lived in constant fear of ruin; when the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous cause, Ping pledged himself to him.

sentences.zh: 從平鄴，破四胡於韓陵。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Ye and breaking the Four Huns at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of Ye and the breaking of the Four Huns at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 仲遠既走，以平為東郡大行臺。

translations.literal: After Zhongyuan had fled, Ping was made chief commissioner of the Eastern Commandery circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyuan fled, Ping was made chief commissioner of the Eastern Commandery circuit.

sentences.zh: 軍還，從高祖平尒朱兆。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he followed the Grand Ancestor in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he followed the Grand Ancestor in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 復從領軍婁昭討樊子鵠平之。

translations.literal: Again he followed the army commander Lou Zhao in campaigning against and pacifying Fan Zihu.
translations.idiomatic: Again he followed the army commander Lou Zhao in campaigning against Fan Zihu and pacifying him.

sentences.zh: 授使持節、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was granted bearer of the staff of authority and made governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted bearer of the staff of authority and made governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 高仲密之叛，平從高祖破周文帝於邙山。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Ping followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Ping followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 武定初，除廓州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, he was appointed governor of Kuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding he was appointed governor of Kuo Province.

sentences.zh: 五年，加儀同三司，鎮河陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the rank equal to the Three Excellencies and garrisoned Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was given rank equal to the three excellencies and garrisoned Heyang.

sentences.zh: 八年，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his noble rank was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 天保初，授兗州刺史，尋加開府，別封臨洮縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was appointed governor of Yan Province; soon given the seal of opening an office and separately enfeoffed Viscount of Lintao County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed governor of Yan Province; soon he was given the seal of opening an office and separately enfeoffed viscount of Lintao County.

sentences.zh: 三年，與諸將南討江淮，克陽平郡。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with various generals he campaigned south against the Yangtze and Huai regions and captured Yangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, together with other generals, he campaigned south into the Yangtze and Huai country and captured Yangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 陳人攻圍廣陵，詔平統河南諸軍赴援，陳人退，乃還。

translations.literal: When Chen forces besieged Guangling, an edict made Ping command all armies south of the river in relief; the Chen forces withdrew, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen forces besieged Guangling, an edict put Ping in command of all armies south of the river for relief; the Chen men withdrew, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，卒於州，時年五十一。

translations.literal: In summer of the fifth year he died in the province, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year he died in office, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈瀛滄幽三州軍事、瀛州刺史、中書監，謚曰莊惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted military affairs of the three provinces of Ying, Cang, and You, governor of Ying Province, and director of the Palace Secretary; posthumous title Zhuanghui.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted military affairs over Ying, Cang, and You provinces, governor of Ying Province, and director of the palace secretary; posthumous title Zhuanghui.

sentences.zh: 子孝中嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozhong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozhong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 弟長乂。

translations.literal: His younger brother Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Changyi.

sentences.zh: 武平末，侍中、開府儀同三司，封新寧王。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was palace attendant, grand master equal in rank to the Three Excellencies with an office, enfeoffed Prince of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was palace attendant, grand master equal in rank to the three excellencies with an office, and enfeoffed prince of Xining.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，上柱國，卒於涇州長史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was pillar of state and died as chief administrator of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was pillar of state and died while serving as chief administrator of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 雖無他伎，前在官以清幹著稱。

translations.literal: Though he possessed no other special skill, in earlier service he was renowned for integrity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had no other special talent, in earlier service he was known for integrity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 步大汗薩

translations.literal: Buda Hansa
translations.idiomatic: Buda Hansa

sentences.zh: 步大汗薩，太安狄那人也。

translations.literal: Buda Hansa was a man of Dina in Taian.
translations.idiomatic: Buda Hansa was a man of Dina in Taian.

sentences.zh: 曾祖榮，仕魏歷金門、化正二郡太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong served Wei and successively held the governorships of the two commanderies of Jinmen and Huazheng.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong served Wei and in turn held the governorships of Jinmen and Huazheng.

sentences.zh: 父居，龍驤將軍、領民別將。

translations.literal: His father Ju was General of Soaring Dragon and separate commander of tribally enrolled forces.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju was general of soaring dragon and separate commander of tribally enrolled forces.

sentences.zh: 正光末，六鎮反亂，薩乃將家避難南下，奔尒朱榮於秀容。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang the Six Garrisons rose in rebellion; Hansa then led his family south to seek refuge and went to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang the Six Garrisons rose in rebellion; Hansa led his family south to seek refuge and went to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 後從榮入洛，以軍功除揚武軍帳內統軍，賜爵江夏子。

translations.literal: Later he followed Rong into Luoyang and, for military merit, was appointed camp commander within the Yangwu Army, enfeoffed Viscount of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Rong into Luoyang and, for military merit, was appointed camp commander within the Yangwu Army and enfeoffed viscount of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 從平葛榮，累前後功，加鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Ge Rong; accumulating his successive merits, he was made General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of Ge Rong; with merit accumulated over many campaigns, he was made general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 榮死後，從尒朱兆入洛，補帳內大都督，從兆拒戰於韓陵。

translations.literal: After Rong died, he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang, was appointed grand commander within the camp, and followed Zhao in resisting battle at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong died, he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang, was appointed grand commander within the camp, and followed Zhao in resisting at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 兆敗，薩以所部降。

translations.literal: When Zhao was defeated, Hansa surrendered with the force under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated, Hansa surrendered with the troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為第三領民酋長，累遷秦州鎮城都督、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor made him third tribally enrolled chieftain; he was successively promoted to garrison commander of Qin Province's fort and governor of Northern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor made him third tribally enrolled chieftain; he rose in stages to garrison commander of Qin Province's fort and governor of Northern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 天平中，轉東壽陽三泉都督。

translations.literal: During Tianping he was transferred to area commander of the three springs of Eastern Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was transferred to area commander of the three springs of Eastern Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 元象中，行燕州，累遷臨川領民大都督，賜爵長廣伯。

translations.literal: During Yuanxiang he acted as governor of Yan Province; he was successively promoted to grand commander of tribally enrolled forces of Linchuan and enfeoffed Baron of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanxiang he acted as governor of Yan Province; he rose in stages to grand commander of tribally enrolled forces of Linchuan and was enfeoffed baron of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 時茹茹寇鈔，屢為邊害，高祖撫納之，遣薩將命。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran raided and plundered, repeatedly doing border harm; the Grand Ancestor soothed and received them and dispatched Hansa to carry the mission.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran raided the borders again and again; the Grand Ancestor sought to soothe and win them over and dispatched Hansa on the mission.

sentences.zh: 還，拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed equal in rank to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed equal in rank to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 出為五城大都督，鎮河陽。

translations.literal: He went out as grand commander of Wucheng and garrisoned Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand commander of Wucheng and garrisoned Heyang.

sentences.zh: 又加車騎大將軍、開府，進封行唐縣公，減勃海三百戶以增其封。

translations.literal: He was additionally made grand general of chariots and cavalry and given an office; his enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Xingtang County, with three hundred households from Bohai reduced to augment his fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made grand general of chariots and cavalry and given an office; his enfeoffment was advanced to duke of Xingtang County, with three hundred households from Bohai taken to augment his fief.

sentences.zh: 仍授晉州刺史，別封安陵縣男，邑二百戶，加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed governor of Jin Province, separately enfeoffed Baron of Anling County with a fief of two hundred households, and made grand general of fast cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed governor of Jin Province, separately enfeoffed baron of Anling County with a fief of two hundred households, and made grand general of fast cavalry.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，改封義陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his enfeoffment was changed to duke of Yiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 慕容儼

translations.literal: Murong Yan
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yan

sentences.zh: 慕容儼，字恃德，清都成安人，慕容廆之後也。

translations.literal: Murong Yan, styled Shide, was a man of Cheng'an in Qingdu and a descendant of Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yan, styled Shide, was a man of Cheng'an in Qingdu and a descendant of Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 父叱頭，魏南頓太守，身長一丈，腰帶九尺。

translations.literal: His father Chitou was governor of Nandun in Wei; he stood ten chi in height, his belt nine chi long.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chitou had been governor of Nandun in Wei — a man ten chi tall, with a belt nine chi long.

sentences.zh: 武平初，追贈開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射、持節、都督滄、恒二州軍事、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was posthumously granted grand master equal in rank to the Three Excellencies with an office, left vice director of the masters of writing, bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs of Cang and Heng provinces, and governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he was posthumously granted grand master equal in rank to the three excellencies with an office, left vice director of the masters of writing, bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs over Cang and Heng provinces, and governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 儼容貌出群，衣冠甚偉，不好讀書，頗學兵法，工騎射。

translations.literal: Yan's appearance surpassed the crowd; his bearing in cap and robes was very imposing. He did not care for reading books but studied military arts considerably and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's looks stood out from the crowd; in cap and robes he cut an imposing figure. He cared little for books but studied the art of war and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 正光中，魏河間王元琛率衆救壽春，辟儼左廂軍主，以戰功賞帛五十疋。

translations.literal: During Zhengguang, Prince Hejian of Wei Yuanchen led troops to relieve Shouyang and summoned Yan as commander of the left wing; for battle merit he was rewarded with fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengguang, Prince Hejian of Wei, Yuanchen, led troops to relieve Shouyang and summoned Yan as commander of the left wing; for battle merit he was rewarded with fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 軍次西硤石，因解渦陽之圍，平倉陵城、荊山戍。

translations.literal: The army halted at West Xiashi; thereby he relieved the siege of Woyang and pacified Cangling City and the Jingshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at West Xiashi; there he lifted the siege of Woyang and pacified Cangling City and the Jingshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 梁遣將鄭僧等要戰，儼擊之，斬其將蕭喬，梁人奔遁。

translations.literal: Liang dispatched General Zheng Seng and others to offer battle; Yan attacked them, beheaded their general Xiao Qiao, and the Liang men fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Liang dispatched General Zheng Seng and others to offer battle; Yan struck them, beheaded their general Xiao Qiao, and the Liang men broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 又襲破王神念等軍，擒二百餘人，神念僅以身免。

translations.literal: Again he launched a surprise attack and broke the army of Wang Shennian and others, capturing more than two hundred men; Shennian barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Again he launched a surprise attack and broke the army of Wang Shennian and others, taking more than two hundred prisoners; Shennian barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 三年，梁遣將攻東豫州，大都督元寶掌討之。

translations.literal: In the third year Liang dispatched generals to attack Eastern Yu Province; Grand Commander Yuan Baozhang campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liang dispatched generals against Eastern Yu Province; Grand Commander Yuan Baozhang was sent to repel them.

sentences.zh: 儼為別將。

translations.literal: Yan served as separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served as separate commander.

sentences.zh: 鄭海珍與戰，斬其軍主朱僧珍、軍副秦太。

translations.literal: At Zhenghai he joined battle, beheading their army commander Zhu Sengzhen and deputy army commander Qin Tai.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenghai he joined battle and beheaded their army commander Zhu Sengzhen and deputy army commander Qin Tai.

sentences.zh: 又擊賊王茍於陽夏，平之。

translations.literal: Again he struck the bandit Wang Gou at Yangxia and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Again he struck the bandit Wang Gou at Yangxia and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，尒朱榮入洛，授儼京畿南面都督。

translations.literal: During Xiaochang, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and appointed Yan southern commander of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and appointed Yan southern commander of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 永安中，西荊州為梁將曹義宗所圍，儼應募赴之。

translations.literal: During Yong'an, Western Jing Province was besieged by the Liang general Cao Yizong; Yan answered the call and went to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an, Western Jing Province was besieged by the Liang general Cao Yizong; Yan answered the call and marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 時北育太守宋帶劍謀叛，儼乃輕騎出其不意，直至城下，語云：「大軍已到，太守何不迎？

translations.literal: At that time the governor of Beiyu, Song Daijian, plotted rebellion; Yan then led light cavalry by surprise, going straight to the foot of the city wall, and said: "The great army has already arrived — why does the governor not come out to greet them?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the governor of Beiyu, Song Daijian, plotted rebellion; Yan led light cavalry by surprise straight to the foot of the wall and called out: "The great army has already arrived — why does the governor not come out to greet us?

sentences.zh: 」帶劍造次惶恐不知所為，便出迎，儼即執之，一郡遂定。

translations.literal: " Daijian, startled and terrified, knew not what to do and thereupon came out to greet him; Yan immediately seized him, and the whole commandery was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Startled and at a loss, Daijian came out to greet him; Yan seized him on the spot, and the whole commandery was settled.

sentences.zh: 又破梁將馬元達、蔡天起、柳白嘉等，累有功。

translations.literal: Again he broke the Liang generals Ma Yuanda, Cai Tianqi, and Liu Baijia, accumulating merit time and again.
translations.idiomatic: Again he broke the Liang generals Ma Yuanda, Cai Tianqi, and Liu Baijia, winning merit again and again.

sentences.zh: 除強弩將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Powerful Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general of powerful crossbows.

sentences.zh: 與梁將王玄真、董當門等戰，並破之，解穰城圍，克復南陽、新鄉。

translations.literal: Joining battle with the Liang generals Wang Xuanzhen, Dong Dangmen, and others, he broke them all, relieved the siege of Rang City, and recovered Nanyang and Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: Joining battle with the Liang generals Wang Xuanzhen, Dong Dangmen, and others, he broke them all, lifted the siege of Rang City, and recovered Nanyang and Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 轉積射將軍，持節、豫州防城大都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Accumulated Shots, bearer of the staff of authority, and grand commander of fortification defense in Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of accumulated shots, bearer of the staff of authority, and grand commander of fortification defense in Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 尒朱敗，與豫州刺史李恩歸高祖。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan was defeated, together with Governor Li En of Yu Province he submitted to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan fell, he and Governor Li En of Yu Province submitted to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 以勳累遷安東將軍、高梁太守，轉五城太守、東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: For successive merits he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Gaoliang, transferred to governor of Wucheng and governor of Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: For successive merits he was promoted to general who pacifies the east and governor of Gaoliang, then transferred to governor of Wucheng and governor of Eastern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，西魏荊州刺史郭鸞率衆攻儼，拒守二百餘日，晝夜力戰，大破鸞軍，追斬三百餘級，又擒西魏刺史郭他。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Shaye, Guo Luan, governor of Jing Province in Western Wei, led troops to attack Yan; Yan held out in defense for more than two hundred days, fighting day and night at full strength; he inflicted a great defeat on Luan's army, pursued and beheaded more than three hundred men, and again captured Guo Ta, governor of Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Shaye, Guo Luan, governor of Jing Province in Western Wei, led troops against Yan; Yan held the city for more than two hundred days, fighting day and night without rest; he broke Luan's army utterly, pursued and beheaded more than three hundred men, and captured Guo Ta, another Western Wei governor.

sentences.zh: 時諸州多有翻陷，唯儼獲全。

translations.literal: At that time many provinces turned and fell, but Yan alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many provinces turned and fell, but Yan alone held firm.

sentences.zh: 進號鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Suppresses the South.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was advanced to general who suppresses the south.

sentences.zh: 武定三年，率師解襄州圍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuding he led troops to lift the siege of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuding he led troops to raise the siege of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 頻使茹茹。

translations.literal: He was frequently sent on missions to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly dispatched on diplomatic missions to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 又從攻玉壁，賜帛七百疋並衣帽等。

translations.literal: He again followed in the attack on Yubi and was granted seven hundred bolts of silk together with hats and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the attack on Yubi and was rewarded with seven hundred bolts of silk, hats, and clothing.

sentences.zh: 五年，鎮河橋五城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he garrisoned the five cities at River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was stationed at the five cities of River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 侯景叛，儼擊陳郡賊，獲景麾下庫狄曷賴及偽暑太守鄭道合、兗州刺史王彥夏、行臺狄暢等，擒斬百餘級。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Yan attacked the bandits of Chen Commandery and captured Kudi Helai under Jing's command, together with falsely appointed Governor Zheng Daohe, Yanzhou Inspector Wang Yanxia, Mobile Circuit Commissioner Di Chang, and others; more than a hundred were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Murong Yan struck the rebel forces in Chen Commandery and captured Kudi Helai of Hou Jing's following, together with the falsely appointed governor Zheng Daohe, Yanzhou inspector Wang Yanxia, mobile circuit commissioner Di Chang, and others — more than a hundred heads taken in all.

sentences.zh: 旋軍項城，又擒景偽署刺史辛光及蔡遵，並其部下二千人。

translations.literal: Wheeling his army to Xiangcheng, he again captured Jing's falsely appointed Inspector Xin Guang and Cai Zun, together with two thousand of their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Xiangcheng, he again seized Hou Jing's pseudo-inspector Xin Guang and Cai Zun, together with two thousand of their troops.

sentences.zh: 六年，除譙州刺史，屢有戰功，多所降附。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Governor of Qiao Province; he repeatedly won distinction in battle and brought many to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made governor of Qiao Province; he won repeated victories and brought many defectors over.

sentences.zh: 七年，又除膠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed Governor of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made governor of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao he was appointed Opening-Establishment Honor Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was granted opening-establishment honor equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 六年，梁司徒陸法和、儀同宋茝蒨等率其部下以郢州城內附。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Liang Minister over the Masses Lu Fahé, Equal-in-Rank Song Chihui, and others led their followers in submitting from within Ying Province city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Liang minister over the masses Lu Fahé, equal-in-rank Song Chihui, and others brought their followers over from within the walls of Ying city.

sentences.zh: 時清河王岳帥師江上，乃集諸軍議曰：「城在江外，人情尚梗，必須才略兼濟，忠勇過人，可受此寄耳。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qinghe Yue commanded troops on the river; he gathered the armies in council and said: "The city lies beyond the river; hearts there are still recalcitrant. One must have both talent and stratagem, with loyalty and courage surpassing other men — only such a one can receive this charge."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Qinghe Yue had troops on the Yangzi and called the commanders together. "The city stands beyond the river," he said, "and hearts there are still hard to win. It will take a man who combines talent with stratagem, whose loyalty and courage outmatch all others — only such a man can hold this trust."

sentences.zh: 」衆咸共推儼。

translations.literal: All together recommended Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly unanimously pointed to Murong Yan.

sentences.zh: 岳以為然，遂遣鎮郢城。

translations.literal: Yue agreed and thereupon dispatched him to garrison Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Yue assented and sent Yan to hold Ying city.

sentences.zh: 始入，便為梁大都督侯瑱、任約率水陸軍奄至城下。

translations.literal: As soon as he entered, Liang Grand Commander-in-Chief Hou Zhen and Ren Yue led land and river forces and suddenly arrived beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he entered when Liang grand commander Hou Zhen and Ren Yue swept up by land and water to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 儼隨方禦備，瑱等不能克。

translations.literal: Yan met each threat with appropriate defense; Zhen and the others could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yan answered each threat as it came; Zhen and his fellows could not break him.

sentences.zh: 又於上流鸚鵡洲上造荻洪竟數里，以塞船路。

translations.literal: They also constructed a reed barrier several li long on Parrot Isle upstream to block the shipping lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream at Parrot Isle they built a reed boom several li long to choke off the river route.

sentences.zh: 人信阻絕，城守孤懸，衆情危懼，儼導以忠義，又悅以安之。

translations.literal: Communications with the outside were cut off; the city's defense hung alone; the crowd grew fearful — Yan guided them with loyalty and righteousness, and also soothed and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from the world, the garrison clung to an isolated city, and fear spread through the ranks. Yan led them with talk of loyalty and duty, and won them back with kindness until they steadied.

sentences.zh: 城中先有神祠一所，俗號城隍神，公私每有祈禱。

translations.literal: Within the city there was already a spirit shrine, popularly called the City God; both public and private made prayers there.
translations.idiomatic: The city already held a shrine to what people called the City God; officials and commoners alike prayed there.

sentences.zh: 於是順士卒之心，乃相率祈請，冀獲冥佑。

translations.literal: Thereupon, following the hearts of the officers and soldiers, they went together to pray, hoping to obtain invisible aid.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the mood of his troops, he led them in common prayer, hoping for protection from beyond the veil.

sentences.zh: 須臾，衝風欻起，驚濤湧激，漂斷荻洪。

translations.literal: In a moment a rushing wind suddenly arose; startled waves surged and swept away the reed barrier.
translations.idiomatic: In an instant a tearing wind sprang up; waves roared and tore the reed boom apart.

sentences.zh: 約復以鐵鎖連治，防禦彌切。

translations.literal: Yue again joined iron chains in a continuous barrier; the blockade grew tighter still.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue linked iron chains in a fresh barrier; the blockade tightened.

sentences.zh: 儼還共祈請，風浪夜驚，復以斷絕，如此者再三。

translations.literal: Yan again prayed with them together; wind and waves startled the night and once more broke it apart — this happened again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Yan prayed with them again; that night wind and waves rose in fury and snapped the chains once more — and so it went, again and again.

sentences.zh: 城人大喜，以為神功。

translations.literal: The people of the city rejoiced greatly and took it for divine merit.
translations.idiomatic: The city erupted in joy and called it the work of the gods.

sentences.zh: 瑱移軍於城北，造柵置營，焚燒坊郭，產業皆盡。

translations.literal: Zhen shifted his army to the north of the city, built palisades and set up camps, and burned the wards — every estate was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen shifted north of the walls, threw up palisades and camps, and burned the suburbs until nothing was left standing.

sentences.zh: 約將戰士萬餘人，各持攻具，於城南置營壘，南北合勢。

translations.literal: Yue commanded more than ten thousand fighting men, each bearing siege engines; south of the city he set up camps and joined forces north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue brought more than ten thousand warriors with siege gear and pitched camp south of the city, closing a pincer from north and south.

sentences.zh: 儼乃率步騎出城奮擊，大破之，擒五百餘人。

translations.literal: Yan then led infantry and cavalry out of the city in a fierce charge, routed them greatly, and captured more than five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Yan led infantry and cavalry out in a furious sally, broke them utterly, and took more than five hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 先是郢城卑下，兼土疏頹壞，儼更修繕城雉，多作大樓。

translations.literal: Earlier Ying city had been low-lying; its earth was loose and the walls crumbling — Yan rebuilt the parapets and raised many great towers.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had been a low, ramshackle place with walls of crumbling earth. Yan rebuilt the ramparts and raised tall fighting towers.

sentences.zh: 又造船艦，水陸備具，工無暫闕。

translations.literal: He also built war vessels; land and river forces were fully equipped, and labor never paused.
translations.idiomatic: He built warships too; land and river were readied for war, and the work crews never rested.

sentences.zh: 蕭循又率衆五萬，與瑱、約合軍，夜來攻擊。

translations.literal: Xiao Xun again led fifty thousand men, joined armies with Zhen and Yue, and came by night to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xun mustered fifty thousand more, combined with Zhen and Yue, and struck at night.

sentences.zh: 儼與將士力戰終夕，至明，約等乃退。

translations.literal: Yan and his officers and soldiers fought with all their strength through the night; at dawn Yue and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his men fought through the night; at first light, Ren Yue and the rest fell back.

sentences.zh: 追斬瑱驍將張白石首，瑱以千金贖之，不與。

translations.literal: Pursuing, he beheaded Zhen's fierce general Zhang Baishi; Zhen offered a thousand in gold to ransom him — Yan refused.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuit he cut down Zhen's champion Zhang Baishi. Zhen offered a thousand in gold for the head — Yan would not take it.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，瑱、約等又相與並力，悉衆攻圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Zhen, Yue, and the others again joined forces and assaulted the siege with their entire host.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhen and Ren Yue joined again and threw every man they had at the walls.

sentences.zh: 城中食少，糧運阻絕，無以為計，唯煮槐楮、桑葉並紵根、水萍、葛、艾等草及靴、皮帶、筋角等物而食之。

translations.literal: Food in the city was scarce; grain convoys were cut off with no remedy — they could only boil pagoda tree, paper mulberry leaves, ramie roots, duckweed, kudzu, mugwort, and the like, together with boots, leather belts, sinews and horns, and eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions ran low; grain could not get through. With no other recourse they boiled pagoda bark, mulberry leaves, ramie root, duckweed, kudzu, mugwort — boots, belts, sinew and horn — and ate whatever would cook.

sentences.zh: 人有死者，即取其肉，火別分噉，唯留骸骨。

translations.literal: When a man died, they immediately took his flesh, divided it with fire, and ate — leaving only the bones.
translations.idiomatic: When a man died, they cut his flesh, cooked it, and shared it out, leaving only the bones.

sentences.zh: 儼猶申令將士，信賞必罰，分甘同苦，死生以之。

translations.literal: Yet Yan still announced orders to officers and soldiers: rewards given in faith, punishments surely carried out; sweetness shared, bitterness shared — life and death together.
translations.idiomatic: Even then Yan kept discipline among his men: promised rewards he paid, promised punishments he delivered; whatever sweetness or bitterness remained, he shared it — life and death alike.

sentences.zh: 自正月至於六月，人無異志。

translations.literal: From the first month to the sixth, none wavered in will.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month through the sixth, not one man broke faith.

sentences.zh: 後蕭方智立，遣使請和。

translations.literal: Later, when Xiao Fangzhi was enthroned, he dispatched envoys requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Fangzhi came to the throne and sent envoys suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 顯祖以城在江表，據守非便，有詔還之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan, because the city lay on the southern bank of the river and holding it was inconvenient, issued an edict recalling it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang, judging that a city south of the river was too hard to hold, ordered the garrison withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 儼望帝，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Yan looked upon the emperor and grieved beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan saw the emperor again, grief overwhelmed him.

sentences.zh: 帝呼令至前，執其手，持儼鬚鬢，脫帽看髪，嘆息久之。

translations.literal: The emperor called him forward, took his hand, held Yan's beard and side whiskers, removed his hat to look at his hair, and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called him forward, clasped his hand, lifted Yan's beard, took off his hat to see how his hair had turned, and sighed a long while.

sentences.zh: 謂儼曰：「觀卿容貌，朕不復相識，自古忠烈，豈能過此！

translations.literal: He said to Yan: "Looking at your face, I no longer recognize you. Loyal heroes since antiquity — could any surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to Yan, "Looking at you, I would not know you. Among the loyal and fierce of every age — who has surpassed this?"

sentences.zh: 」儼對曰：「臣恃陛下威靈，得申愚節，不屈豎子，重奉聖顏。

translations.literal: Yan replied: "Your servant relied on Your Majesty's august power and attained my humble loyalty; I did not bow to those petty fellows and again behold the sacred countenance."
translations.idiomatic: Yan answered, "I leaned on Your Majesty's majesty to keep my poor pledge — I did not bow to those whelps, and here I stand before you again."

sentences.zh: 今雖夕死，沒而無恨。

translations.literal: Though I die tonight, in death I will have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Even if I die tonight, I will go without regret."

sentences.zh: 」帝嗟稱不已。

translations.literal: The emperor exclaimed praise without end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him again and again.

sentences.zh: 除趙州刺史，進伯為公，賜帛一千疋、錢十萬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Zhao Province; his rank as Baron was advanced to Duke, and he was granted one thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yan was made governor of Zhao Province, raised from baron to duke, and given a thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 尒朱將帥，義旗建後歸順立功者，武威牒舍樂、代郡范舍樂亦致通顯。

translations.literal: Among Erzhu generals who after the righteous banner was raised submitted and achieved merit, Wuwei Dieshele and Dai's Fan Shele also reached eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Among Erzhu commanders who came over after the righteous standard was raised and won distinction — Wuwei Dieshele and Fan Shele of Dai also rose to high rank.

sentences.zh: 牒舍樂，少從尒朱榮為軍主、統軍，後西河領民都督。

translations.literal: Dieshele in youth followed Erzhu Rong as army commander and army leader; later he was Registered-Tribal Commander of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Dieshele followed Erzhu Rong from youth as army commander and army leader, and later served as registered-tribal commander of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆敗，率衆歸高祖，拜鎮西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao was defeated, he led his host to submit to the Grand Ancestor and was appointed General Who Stabilizes the West and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao fell, he brought his troops to Gao Huan and was made general who stabilizes the west and grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 以都督隸侯景，破賀拔勝於穰城。

translations.literal: As a commander he served under Hou Jing and defeated Helü Sheng at Rang city.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Hou Jing as commander, he defeated Helü Sheng at Rang.

sentences.zh: 又與諸將討平青、兗、荊三州，拜鎮西將軍、營州刺史。

translations.literal: He again with the generals suppressed and pacified the three provinces of Qing, Yan, and Jing, and was appointed General Who Stabilizes the West and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: With other generals he pacified Qing, Yan, and Jing provinces and was made general who stabilizes the west and governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封漢中郡公。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Duke of Hanzhong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was enfeoffed duke of Hanzhong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後因戰沒於關中。

translations.literal: Later he fell in battle in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell in battle in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 范舍樂，有武藝，筋力絕人。

translations.literal: Fan Shele had martial skill; his strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shele was skilled in arms, with strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 魏末，從崔暹、李崇等征討有功，授統軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he followed Cui Xuan, Li Chong, and others on punitive campaigns with merit and was appointed army leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Wei he followed Cui Xuan and Li Chong on campaigns, won merit, and was made army leader.

sentences.zh: 後入尒朱榮軍中，頻有戰功，授都督。

translations.literal: Later he entered Erzhu Rong's army; he frequently had military merit and was appointed commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered Erzhu Rong's ranks, won repeated victories, and was made commander.

sentences.zh: 後隨尒朱兆破步藩於梁都。

translations.literal: Later he followed Erzhu Zhao in defeating Bu Fan at Liangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Zhao to break Bu Fan at Liangdu.

sentences.zh: 高祖義旗舉，棄兆歸信都。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous banner, he abandoned Zhao and returned to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous banner, he abandoned Zhao and joined him at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 從高祖破兆於廣阿、韓陵，並有功，賜爵平舒男。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Ancestor he defeated Zhao at Guang'a and Hanling, both with merit, and was granted the title Baron of Pingshu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in defeating Zhao at Guang'a and Hanling, and for merit on both fields was enfeoffed baron of Pingshu.

sentences.zh: 每從征役，多有克捷。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed on campaign, he often won victories.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he fought, he often carried the day.

sentences.zh: 除相府左廂大都督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Commander of the Chancellor's Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commander of the chancellor's left wing.

sentences.zh: 尋出為東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Governor of Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as governor of Eastern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣事，封平舒縣侯，拜儀同。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent succeeded to affairs he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingshu County and appointed Equal-in-Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took up power he was enfeoffed marquis of Pingshu County and made equal-in-rank.

sentences.zh: 天保中，進位開府。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era his rank was advanced to opening-establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he was promoted to opening-establishment rank.

sentences.zh: 又有代人庫狄伏連，字仲山，少以武幹事尒朱榮，至直閤將軍。

translations.literal: There was also Kudí Fulian of Dai, styled Zhongshan; in youth for martial capacity he served Erzhu Rong and reached Direct Attendant General.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Kudí Fulian of Dai, styled Zhongshan — a man who from youth served Erzhu Rong for his martial worth and rose to direct attendant general.

sentences.zh: 後從高祖建義，賜爵蛇丘男。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Grand Ancestor in establishing righteousness and was granted the title Baron of Sheqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising the revolt and was enfeoffed baron of Sheqiu.

sentences.zh: 世宗輔政，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent assisted in government, he was transferred to Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng guided affairs of state, he was made martial guard general.

sentences.zh: 天保初，儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao he held honor equal to the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he held honor equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 四年，除鄭州刺史，尋加開府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Governor of Zheng Province; soon opening-establishment rank was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made governor of Zheng Province; opening-establishment rank followed shortly after.

sentences.zh: 伏連質樸，勤於公事。

translations.literal: Fulian was plain and sincere and diligent in public business.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian was plain-spoken and diligent in office.

sentences.zh: 直衛官闕，曉夕不離帝所，以此見知。

translations.literal: When the direct guard posts were vacant, dawn and dusk he did not leave the emperor's side — for this he won notice.
translations.idiomatic: When direct guard duty fell to him, he stayed at the emperor's side from dawn to dusk — and won favor for it.

sentences.zh: 鄙吝愚狠，無治民政術。

translations.literal: Mean, stingy, foolish and harsh — he had no art of governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was petty, tight-fisted, coarse and cruel, with no gift for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 及居州任，專事聚斂。

translations.literal: When he held provincial office, his sole business was accumulation and extraction.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial office his only business was squeezing the people dry.

sentences.zh: 性又嚴酷，不識士流。

translations.literal: By nature he was also harsh and cruel and did not recognize genteel society.
translations.idiomatic: His nature ran harsh and cruel; he had no patience for cultivated men.

sentences.zh: 開府參軍多是衣冠士族，伏連加以捶撻，逼遣築墻。

translations.literal: Opening-establishment staff officers were mostly genteel clansmen in official dress — Fulian beat them with flails and drove them to build walls.
translations.idiomatic: His opening-establishment aides were mostly men of gentle birth — Fulian flogged them and drove them out to raise walls.

sentences.zh: 武平中，封宜都郡王，除領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was enfeoffed Prince of Yidu Commandery and appointed Colonel Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he was enfeoffed prince of Yidu Commandery and made colonel director of the army.

sentences.zh: 尋與瑯琊王儼殺和士開，伏誅。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Prince of Langya Yan, he killed He Shikai and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, together with Gao Yan, Prince of Langya, he killed He Shikai and paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 伏連家口有百數，盛夏之日，料以倉料二升，不給鹽菜，常有饑色。

translations.literal: Fulian's household numbered in the hundreds; in midsummer days he rationed them two sheng of storehouse grain, gave no salt or vegetables, and they often showed hunger in their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian kept a household of a hundred mouths. Even in high summer he rationed them two sheng of stored grain apiece, with no salt or greens — hunger showed on every face.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，親表稱賀，妻為設豆餅。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice, kin and friends offered congratulations; his wife set out bean cakes.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice kith and kin came to offer felicitations; his wife served bean cakes.

sentences.zh: 伏連問此豆因何而得，妻對向於食馬豆中分減充用，伏連大怒，典馬、掌食之人並加杖罰，積年賜物，藏在別庫，遣侍婢一人專掌管籥。

translations.literal: Fulian asked whence these beans came; his wife replied that she had taken them by division from the horse-feed beans — Fulian flew into a rage; the horse stewards and food keepers were all flogged. Gifts accumulated over years he stored in a separate treasury, sending one maidservant exclusively to keep the keys.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian demanded to know where the beans had come from. His wife confessed she had skimmed them from the horse-feed stores. He flew into a rage and had the stable and pantry stewards flogged. Years of imperial gifts he locked in a separate vault, with a single maid holding the keys.

sentences.zh: 每入庫檢閱，必語妻子云：「此是官物，不得輒用。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered the storehouse to inspect, he invariably told wife and children: "These are official goods — you must not use them at will."
translations.idiomatic: Each time he inspected the vault he told his wife and children, "These are state goods. You are not to touch them."

sentences.zh: 」至是薄錄，並歸天府。

translations.literal: At this time an inventory was made and all was returned to the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After his execution an inventory was taken and everything went back to the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祖霸業始基，招集英勇。

translations.literal: The historian writes: When the Grand Ancestor's hegemonic enterprise was first laid, he gathered the brave.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Gao Huan first laid the foundations of empire, he gathered the brave.

sentences.zh: 張瓊等雖識非先覺，而運屬時來，驅馳戎旅，日不暇給，義宣禦侮，契協寵圖，臨敵制勝，有足稱也。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiong and the others, though their discernment fell short of foresight, met the fortune of their time; they raced through martial campaigns with never a day's respite, loyally proclaiming resistance to insult, in accord with the favored design — facing the enemy and securing victory, they deserve mention.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiong and the rest were no prophets — yet fortune favored their hour. They spent their days in the saddle without rest, holding the line with loyal hearts, serving the founding design — and when steel met steel they prevailed. That much deserves record.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗兵機武略，在世見推。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong's military timing and martial stratagem were praised in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong's grasp of war and martial stratagem won esteem in his own day.

sentences.zh: 昔事尒朱，固執忠義，不用范增之言，終見烏江之禍。

translations.literal: In former days he served the Erzhu, holding fast to loyalty and righteousness; he did not heed Fan Zeng's counsel and in the end met calamity at the Wu River.
translations.idiomatic: Once he served the Erzhu clan and clung to loyalty even past reason — he would not take Fan Zeng's advice, and in the end met his Wu River.

sentences.zh: 侯景狼戾，固非後主之臣，末命諸言，實表知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Hou Jing was savage and unruly — no true minister to the Later Sovereign; his final testamentary words truly showed discernment in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was savage and untamable — no fit servant for a later sovereign. His dying words showed a clearer eye for men than his living years.

sentences.zh: 寒山、渦水，往若摧枯，算盡數奇，逢斯厄運，悲夫！

translations.literal: At Hanshan and Guo River — going forth like snapping dry wood; his calculations exhausted, his fortune strange, meeting this calamitous fate — lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: At Hanshan and the Guo River he had gone forth like snapping deadwood — yet fate ran against him, calculations failed, and this bitter end came. Alas!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：霸圖立肇，王業是因。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The hegemonic design was first established; the royal enterprise arose from it.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The hegemonic design was first laid — the royal enterprise grew from that root.

sentences.zh: 偉哉諸將，實曰功臣。

translations.literal: Great are these generals — truly they are meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Great were these generals — true pillars of merit.

sentences.zh: 永懷耿、賈，無累清塵。

translations.literal: Forever remembering Geng and Jia, without burdening the pure dust.
translations.idiomatic: May they stand forever beside Geng and Jia, unburdened by worldly stain.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
